what_its_for: Cysteamine is used to treat a rare inherited disease called cystinosis. In cystinosis, a substance called cystine builds up inside cells and damages your kidneys and other organs. Cysteamine helps break down this buildup and protects your organs from damage.
how_to_take: Take cysteamine exactly as your doctor tells you. Cystagon capsules are usually taken every 6 hours, four times a day, with or without food. Procysbi delayed-release capsules are taken every 12 hours and should NOT be taken with milk or milk-based foods — take it at least 30 minutes before or after dairy. You can open capsules and sprinkle the contents on food (like applesauce) if you have trouble swallowing them whole, but do NOT crush or chew Procysbi capsules. Always swallow with water or juice.
dosing: Your dose is based on your body weight and will be slowly increased by your doctor over time to reduce side effects. A typical maintenance dose is about 1.3 grams per square meter of body surface area per day, divided into doses. Your doctor will determine the exact dose that is right for you. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor. Blood tests will be done regularly to make sure the medicine is working properly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store Cystagon capsules in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Once opened, it can be kept at room temperature up to 77°F (25°C) for up to 30 days. Store Procysbi capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep all forms in a tightly closed container away from light and moisture. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT take Procysbi with milk, formula, yogurt, cheese, or other dairy products, as dairy can affect how the medicine is absorbed. Avoid antacids that contain calcium or magnesium within 2 hours of taking cysteamine. Do not drink alcohol while on this medication. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some drugs can interact with cysteamine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; unusual skin rash, bruising, or skin sores; bone or joint pain; a rash that looks like stretch marks on the skin; problems with walking or movement; vision changes or eye pain; fever or signs of infection; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); blood in the urine or decreased urination; or any serious side effect that worries you. Also call your doctor if you develop a bad smell from your body or breath that bothers you — this is common and your doctor may be able to help.
when_it_works: Cysteamine starts working to lower cystine levels in your cells relatively quickly, but it may take weeks to months before you notice full benefits. Your doctor will monitor your cystine levels with regular blood tests (called leukocyte cystine levels) to check if the medicine is working. It is very important to take this medicine consistently every day — even if you feel well — to keep protecting your kidneys and other organs.
special_populations: Children: Cysteamine is commonly used in infants and young children with cystinosis. Doses are carefully calculated by weight. Parents should contact the doctor immediately if the child shows signs of a reaction. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of cysteamine during pregnancy is not fully known, and the drug may pass into breast milk. Your doctor will help weigh the risks and benefits. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution and close monitoring by your doctor. Elderly: There is limited information on use in elderly patients; your doctor will monitor you closely.
